{{Use dmy dates|date=September 2019}}
'''Anne Elizabeth Magurran''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|CBE|FRSE}} (born 1955) is a British Professor of ecology at [[University of St Andrews]] in [[Scotland]].<ref name=":12">{{Cite web|url=https://risweb.st-andrews.ac.uk/portal/en/persons/anne-magurran(4b27832d-6f10-48f3-9fe8-ac4b8bec6958).html|title=Anne Magurran - University of St Andrews|website=risweb.st-andrews.ac.uk|access-date=2019-03-09}}</ref> She is the author of several books<ref name=":12" /><ref name=":02">{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=tUqzLSUzXxcC|title=Measuring Biological Diversity|last=Magurran|first=Anne E.|date=2004|publisher=Wiley|isbn=9780632056330|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Q5oURmsTv4wC|title=Biological Diversity: Frontiers in Measurement and Assessment|last1=Magurran|first1=Anne E.|last2=McGill|first2=Brian J.|date=2010-11-18|publisher=OUP Oxford|isbn=9780199580668|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":22">{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=U_4DX8vX1xcC|title=Evolution of Biological Diversity|last1=Magurran|first1=Anne E.|last2=Britain)|first2=Royal Society (Great|journal=Current Biology|date=1999|volume=20|issue=13|pages=R545-6|publisher=Oxford University Press|doi=10.1016/j.cub.2010.05.016|pmid=20641176|isbn=9780198503040|s2cid=37059779|language=en}}</ref> on measuring [[biological diversity]], and the importance for quantifying biodiversity for conservation. She has won numerous awards and honors, is regularly consulted for global assessments and analyses of biodiversity and conservation<ref name=":02" /> and her research is often highlighted by journalists.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://blogs.scientificamerican.com/not-bad-science/disproving-hollywood-stereotypes-the-bare-bones-of-piranha-behaviour/|title=Disproving Hollywood Stereotypes: The Bare Bones of Piranha Behaviour|last=Muth|first=Felicity|website=Scientific American Blog Network|language=en|access-date=2019-03-09}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/podcast/episode/needed-info-on-biodiversity-change-over-time/|title=Needed: Info on Biodiversity Change over Time|last=Mirsky|first=Steve|website=Scientific American|language=en|access-date=2019-03-09}}</ref>

Magurran has worked with [[Robert May, Baron May of Oxford|Robert May]] and other leading biologists, including [[Helder Queiroz]], whom she advised. Her research projects often focus on tropical freshwater fish communities - specifically the Trinidadian guppy- in the Neotropics and India.<ref name="Magurran">{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=2WxwxwSlhXYC|title=Evolutionary Ecology: The Trinidadian Guppy|last=Magurran|first=Anne E.|date=2005-08-25|publisher=OUP Oxford|isbn=9780198527855|language=en}}</ref>

== Research and career ==
Magurran completed her PhD at the University of Ulster on the biological diversity of native woodlands in Ireland.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Magurran|first=Anne|date=2010|title=Anne Magurran|journal=Current Biology|language=en|volume=20|issue=13|pages=R545–R546|doi=10.1016/j.cub.2010.05.016|pmid=20641176|s2cid=37059779|doi-access=free|bibcode=2010CBio...20.R545M }}</ref> She then went on to complete postdoctoral work at  [[Bangor University]] and the [[University of Oxford]]. Throughout her career she has used fish communities to study biodiversity, the evolution of [[biodiversity]], and on the role of predation in the evolution of social behaviour. She is now a professor at the [[University of St Andrews]], where she is the university's most cited female scientist.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://scholar.google.co.uk/citations?view_op=view_org&hl=en&org=6411711566900187963 |title=University of St Andrews organization profile |publisher=Open Publishing |date=2019-06-24 |website=Google Scholar |access-date=2019-06-24}}</ref> Globally, she is the second most cited female ecologist <ref>{{cite web |url=https://scholar.google.co.uk/citations?view_op=search_authors&hl=en&mauthors=label:ecology |title=Citation numbers list in ecology |publisher=Open Publishing |date=2019-06-24 |website=Google Scholar |access-date=2019-06-24}}</ref> and evolutionary biologist.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://scholar.google.co.uk/citations?view_op=search_authors&hl=en&mauthors=label:evolution |title=Citation numbers list in evolution |publisher=Open Publishing |date=2019-06-24 |website=Google Scholar |access-date=2019-06-24}}</ref> She is an international counselor and advisor on issues of conservation related to biodiversity and engaged in the UN [[Convention on Biological Diversity]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Magurran|first=Anne E.|date=2010-12-15|title=Q&A: What is biodiversity?|journal=BMC Biology|volume=8|issue=1|pages=145|doi=10.1186/1741-7007-8-145|pmid=21159210|issn=1741-7007|pmc=3002324 |doi-access=free }}</ref> and in the [[World Economic Forum]] in 2018.<ref name=":02" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://erc.europa.eu/event/world-economic-forum-annual-meeting-2018|title=World Economic Forum Annual Meeting 2018 – Davos Summit|date=2018-01-08|website=ERC: European Research Council|language=en|access-date=2019-03-09}}</ref>

Magurran was appointed [[Commander of the Order of the British Empire]] (CBE) in the [[2022 New Year Honours]] for services to biodiversity.<ref>{{London Gazette|issue=63571|supp=y|page=N9|date=1 January 2022}}</ref> 

== Selected awards and honours ==
* 2022 - Distinguished Service Award from the Europe Section of the [[Society for Conservation Biology]] (SCB)
* 2022 - Commander of the Order of the British Empire ([[Order of the British Empire|CBE]])<ref>{{Cite web|date=2022-01-05|title=RSE Fellows included in The New Year Honours 2022|url=https://rse.org.uk/rse-fellows-included-in-the-new-year-honours-2022/|access-date=2022-01-27|website=Royal Society of Edinburgh|language=en-GB}}</ref>
* 2021 - Member of the [[Royal Irish Academy]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ria.ie/news/membership/admittance-day-2021 |title=Admittance Day 2021 |work=Royal Irish Academy |date=21 May 2021 |access-date=2021-05-26}}</ref>
* 2017 - Plenary Talk, Argentinian International Ecology Meeting
* 2014 - Honorary Doctor of Science Degree, [[University of Bergen]]<ref name=":12" />
* 2012 - [[Royal Society]] Wolfson Research Merit Award<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/news/2012/Wolfsons-May-2012/|title=Royal Society announces first round of prestigious Wolfson Research Merit Awards for 2012 {{!}} Royal Society|website=royalsociety.org|language=en-gb|access-date=2019-03-09}}</ref>
* 2006 - Honorary Life Membership, [[Fisheries Society of the British Isles]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fsbi.org.uk/about/medals/|title=Medals|website=Fisheries Society of the British Isles|language=en-GB|access-date=2019-03-09}}</ref>
* 2004 - Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Edinburgh]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rse.org.uk/fellow/anne-magurran/|title=Professor Anne Elizabeth Magurran FRSE|date=2017-05-19|website=The Royal Society of Edinburgh|language=en-GB|access-date=2019-03-09}}</ref>
* 1994 - Scientific Medal, Zoological Society of London<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.zsl.org/about-us/zsl-awards|title=ZSL Awards|website=Zoological Society of London (ZSL)|language=en|access-date=2019-03-09}}</ref>
*
